analysis: The trial succeeded with host-evaluated macro validation HR@10 of 0.5138, versus the supplied parent’s 0.5038 and baseline’s 0.505: gains of 0.0100 and 0.0088 respectively. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.510, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.590, Electronics 0.420, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.535. These results support retaining relative-distance attention bias as a promising change, but one run does not establish causality or statistical significance. Electronics remains the weakest category; category-level improvements cannot be determined without parent category metrics. No test metrics were used.
code_summary: ConvRec uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, eight causal residual convolution blocks with dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8], and two-head causal attention. The change adds jointly learned per-head relative-distance logits using 32 buckets: 16 exact recent-distance buckets and 16 logarithmic older-distance buckets, initialized with mild recency preferences. Training retains sampled-softmax loss with 32 negatives, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, seed 42, and validation-based checkpoint selection. The predictor imports the matching architecture and loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category, preserving all four dataset routes without ensembling.
